scope: Six additive existing-profile narratives and one new named provider within the existing Orange County directory scope. Source-stated only; no clinical verification, human-review or indexing promotion. Exact previously approved portrait entries remain unchanged.

profiles.name: Jenna Lester

claims.text: UCSF's account describes Jenna Lester establishing the Skin of Color Program in 2018 to address the dermatologic care needs of Black and Brown people in Northern California.
claims.excerpt: This program was established by Dr. Jenna Lester to address the dermatologic care needs of Black and Brown people in Northern California.

claims.text: The program brings clinical care together with teaching residents and medical students about caring for patients of different racial and ethnic backgrounds.
claims.excerpt: We work with UCSF learners, including residents and medical students, to teach them the principles of caring for patients who seek care in our program.

claims.text: Its research work examines patterns of disease and treatment affecting those communities, putting health equity alongside clinical practice.
claims.excerpt: We aim to identify patterns of disease and treatment that improves outcomes for Black and Brown patients.

profiles.access: The program tells patients to call 415-353-7800 and ask for the Skin of Color clinic. This is a source-stated routing instruction, not guaranteed appointment capacity, coverage, price or a verified referral requirement.
profiles.portrait: Existing approved local portrait retained; no new image approval.

claims.text: Hannah Braunstein's biography emphasizes continuing personal and professional development alongside her work with trauma and relationships.
claims.excerpt: In her commitment to personal and professional growth and to new developments in theory and practice

claims.text: It describes ongoing study of attachment, neuroscience and mindfulness, and further training in body-focused approaches.
claims.excerpt: Hannah continues to gain clinical expertise in empirically supported trauma treatment, attachment, neuroscience, and mindfulness and meditation practices.

claims.text: The account also records cultural anthropology study at Cornell alongside clinical graduate study in St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: Hannah holds two master’s degrees from Washington University in St. Louis with a clinical focus on mental health and completed her undergraduate work in cultural anthropology at Cornell University.

profiles.name: Yvany Peery

claims.text: Yvany Peery's biography introduces her as a Washington, D.C., native whose education includes Howard University and social-work study at the University of Maryland.
claims.excerpt: A native of Washington, D.C., Ms. Peery has a master’s degree in social work from the University of Maryland and a bachelor’s degree from Howard University.

claims.text: It describes a practice bringing couples work alongside support for people dealing with complex trauma, loss and grief.
claims.excerpt: As an individual therapist, Ms. Peery specializes in working with those who have experienced complex trauma and loss/grief.

claims.text: The same account describes neuro-affirming care and work with heterosexual, gay, lesbian and queer couples.
claims.excerpt: Ms. Peery works with heterosexual couples, gay and lesbian couples, and queer couples.

profiles.portrait: Existing approved local portrait retained; insurance stays practice-scoped.

claims.text: Rachel Bradley Williams's biography describes a career across school and mental-health settings as well as teaching social-work students at Howard and Catholic University.
claims.excerpt: have taught at Howard University, in the School of Social Work and Catholic University, NCSSS (MSW program) as adjunct faculty

claims.text: She describes a strengths-based approach that draws on each client's existing resources.
claims.excerpt: I practice from a strengths-based perspective with the goal of marshaling the inner resources of each client.

claims.text: Her account of whole-person care includes attention to sleep, diet, exercise and mindfulness.
claims.excerpt: For all clients, I believe it is critical to look at the whole person and consider the mind-body connection. This can include examining sleep, diet, and exercise habits in conjunction with mindfulness practices and therapy.

profiles.name: Juris Bunkis

claims.text: The Orange County Plastic Surgery biography describes Juris Bunkis as a surgeon and teacher with a particular interest in facial rejuvenation.
claims.excerpt: His passion is facial rejuvenation and surgery of the face, nose, eyelids and brows.

claims.text: Beyond the practice, it describes volunteer service with the San Bernardino Sheriff's Department and a Southern California consular role for Latvia.
claims.excerpt: he serves as a volunteer deputy with the San Bernardino Sheriff’s Department, the Consul for the Republic of Latvia in Southern California

profiles.portrait: Existing approved local portrait retained; public-service roles are attributed, not independently checked.

profiles.name: Ali Sepehr

claims.text: Ali Sepehr's practice biography explains his decision to concentrate on facial surgery as a belief in focusing deeply on one field.
claims.excerpt: he focused his entire surgical training on the face

claims.text: It traces this specialization through a University of Toronto fellowship and describes teaching fellows, residents and medical students from UC Irvine outside his private practice.
claims.excerpt: Outside of his private practice, he continues to teach fellows, residents, and medical students from the University of California Irvine Medical Center.

claims.text: Consultations are described as conversations about a patient's goals, including questions about training, benefits, risks and recovery.
claims.excerpt: you will receive detailed information about the benefits and risks of your procedure

profiles.portrait: Existing approved local portrait retained; no awards, rankings, certification or outcome assurances imported.
